items.title: SCM lineage refuses invented context
items.statement: The worktree and cross-surface rules explicitly require concrete lineage, partial receipts, and visible partial-lineage degradation rather than fabricated identifiers. This is a strong negative-space guard for misleading operational history.

evidence.exact_quote: - Cross-surface deep links from Orchestrator to Source Control, GitHub Actions, Docker Manager, or Kubernetes owner panels must reopen with stable context after restart. When lineage is incomplete, Orchestrator labels the view as partial lineage; it must never silently omit missing hops or invent repo, worktree, branch, head, receipt, or recovery targets.

items.title: Affected-file summaries lack safety and privacy bounds
items.statement: The blocked worktree card requires an affected-file list or summary but does not define truncation, redaction, symlink handling, path escaping, repository-bound validation, or behavior for extremely large conflict sets. A malicious or merely large path set can leak sensitive names, distort the GUI, or route the operator to the wrong conflict group.
items.impact: Sensitive paths may be exposed and conflict recovery can become misleading or unusable.
items.builder_discretion: Specify canonical path normalization, repo-bound checks, redaction policy, bounded pagination, and an explicit incomplete-summary indicator.

evidence.exact_quote: - blocked worktree cards should include affected file list and an `Open Conflict Assistant` action that routes to the `Source Control > Changes` conflict group through `cmd.source_control.open_conflict`.

items.title: Restart-stable deep links have no invalidation contract
items.statement: Stable reopening after restart is required, but the plan does not define versioning, authorization re-check, deleted worktree behavior, renamed repository behavior, expired receipt handling, or offline fallback. Persisted routes can therefore resurrect stale or unauthorized context.
items.impact: A restored route can present stale truth or expose resources that the current principal may no longer access.
items.builder_discretion: Define a versioned route payload, revalidation at open time, tombstone states, permission checks, and explicit offline/expired degradation.

evidence.exact_quote: - Cross-surface deep links from Orchestrator to Source Control, GitHub Actions, Docker Manager, or Kubernetes owner panels must reopen with stable context after restart. When lineage is incomplete, Orchestrator labels the view as partial lineage; it must never silently omit missing hops or invent repo, worktree, branch, head, receipt, or recovery targets.

items.title: Promotion transitions omit concurrency and rollback semantics
items.statement: Promotion classes enumerate evidence inputs but do not define state transitions, idempotency, competing promoters, evidence freshness, atomicity across lineage and receipt writes, or rollback after a downstream gate partially succeeds.
items.impact: Two promotion attempts can disagree about authority or leave a package or seam in an indeterminate promoted state.
items.builder_discretion: Add an owner transition matrix with compare-and-swap identity, freshness rules, partial-failure receipts, retry idempotency, and compensating transitions.

evidence.exact_quote: - Each promotion class carries exact gate and evidence expectations: promotion gate verdict, lineage refs, required verification evidence, and promotion receipt refs.

items.title: Help entry contract omits accessibility and localization behavior
items.statement: The help template defines content fields but no accessible link semantics, keyboard and screen-reader behavior, locale fallback, translation identity, right-to-left layout expectations, or policy for canonical tokens embedded in translated prose.
items.impact: Help can preserve canonical terms yet remain unusable or ambiguous for assistive-technology and non-English users.
items.builder_discretion: Define accessible navigation semantics, locale/fallback metadata, non-translatable token treatment, and RTL acceptance fixtures.

evidence.exact_quote: - Every help entry follows one template: canonical term, trigger conditions, operator meaning, primary routes, related concepts, and recovery guidance.

items.title: Shared record envelope has no schema evolution or retention contract
items.statement: The envelope states separation and reference families but does not specify schema version, unknown-field behavior, migration, partial writes, referential integrity, retention, deletion, or confidentiality labels for evidence and artifact references.
items.impact: Readers can misinterpret old records, orphan refs, or retain sensitive evidence without a governed lifecycle.
items.builder_discretion: Define versioning, compatibility policy, atomic persistence, reference integrity, retention/deletion, and sensitivity metadata.

evidence.exact_quote: - One shared record envelope carries canonical lineage refs plus artifact and evidence refs.

items.title: Concern lifecycle distinguishes truth change from presentation choice
items.statement: The lifecycle explicitly separates acknowledgement, evidence-backed resolution, rationale-backed dismissal, and reopening on invalidating evidence. It also rejects page-local mutation as durable truth.

evidence.exact_quote: - The concern lifecycle transition matrix is owner prose here: `active -> acknowledged` records operator awareness without changing truth, `active | acknowledged -> resolved` requires evidence that the underlying issue changed, `active | acknowledged -> dismissed` requires a rationale that the concern presentation is intentionally hidden or rejected as actionable framing, and `resolved | dismissed -> active` is the reopen path when new evidence invalidates the prior resolution or dismissal. Resolved and dismissed guard rules require current projection data or direct record revalidation before mutation, and every transition persists through `concern_record` plus `concern_projection` linkage rather than a page-local status flag.

items.title: Concern transitions lack optimistic concurrency and idempotency
items.statement: The matrix specifies allowed semantic transitions but not record revision preconditions, duplicate-command handling, ordering of simultaneous resolve/dismiss/reopen actions, projection write failure, or retry recovery. Current-data revalidation alone does not prevent a time-of-check/time-of-use race.
items.impact: Concurrent actors can overwrite a newer concern disposition or leave record and projection truth inconsistent.
items.builder_discretion: Require expected revision or event sequence, idempotency key, atomic owner write, asynchronous projection repair, and conflict receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: - The concern lifecycle transition matrix is owner prose here: `active -> acknowledged` records operator awareness without changing truth, `active | acknowledged -> resolved` requires evidence that the underlying issue changed, `active | acknowledged -> dismissed` requires a rationale that the concern presentation is intentionally hidden or rejected as actionable framing, and `resolved | dismissed -> active` is the reopen path when new evidence invalidates the prior resolution or dismissal. Resolved and dismissed guard rules require current projection data or direct record revalidation before mutation, and every transition persists through `concern_record` plus `concern_projection` linkage rather than a page-local status flag.

items.title: Dismissal can hide blocking truth without a safety override
items.statement: Dismissal is defined as intentionally hiding or rejecting actionable framing, while blocking_effect is separately modeled. The plan does not say whether a blocking concern may be dismissed, who may do so, what remains visible, or how dependent schedulers react.
items.impact: An operator could hide a concern that still blocks safe execution, producing false-green GUI and scheduler state.
items.builder_discretion: Define blocking dismissal guards, elevated confirmation, persistent residual banners, and downstream consumer semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: - `blocking_effect` stays explicitly separate from `severity`.

items.title: Concern identity is separated from actor roles
items.statement: Owner, creator, and resolver are deliberately distinct, and reassignment does not mutate concern identity. This prevents a common authority and lineage collapse.

evidence.exact_quote: - `owner_kind` / `owner_ref` are separate from `created_by_kind` / `created_by_ref`.

items.title: Resolver authority remains named but not enforceable
items.statement: Resolver authority is declared separate, yet no allowed actor kinds, scope resolution, delegation, revocation, least-privilege rule, or authorization-failure state is specified in this owner contract.
items.impact: Implementations may equate owner, creator, or UI access with resolution permission.
items.builder_discretion: Define resolver grants by action and scope, delegation/revocation, server-side enforcement, and denial receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: - Resolver authority is modeled separately from both owner and creator.

items.title: Minimum concern record omits lifecycle operational fields
items.statement: The minimum shape lacks created/updated timestamps, actor and resolver refs, schema version, record revision, resolution rationale, resolution evidence, retention class, deletion/tombstone status, and projection freshness. Those omissions make concurrency, audit, privacy lifecycle, and support diagnosis under-specified.
items.impact: Concern history cannot be reliably ordered, migrated, expired, or forensically explained.
items.builder_discretion: Extend the required durable shape or normatively bind these fields to the shared envelope.

evidence.exact_quote: - Required fields: `concern_id`, `project_id`, `run_ref`, `scope_ref`, `source_event_ref`, `evidence_refs[]`, `artifact_refs[]`, `lineage_refs[]`, `severity`, `category`, `status`, `visibility_level`, `attention_level`, `chatworthy`, `blocking_effect?`.

items.title: Source-event ingestion trust boundary is absent
items.statement: Raw sightings become source events, but there is no validation, deduplication, provenance authentication, payload-size bound, hostile-markup treatment, or quarantine path before they influence durable records and rendered projections.
items.impact: A provider-controlled sighting can poison concern state, inject misleading UI, or exhaust storage.
items.builder_discretion: Specify trusted ingestion adapters, canonicalization, dedup keys, size limits, sanitization, and quarantine/error receipts.

evidence.exact_quote: - Source events describe raw sightings, records describe durable state, and projections describe rendered consumer views.

items.title: Owner-consumer boundary is descriptive but not executable
items.statement: The owner map delegates cross-document ownership to ContractRefs and notes, yet the PlanUnits shown later declare empty dependencies. No caller/consumer matrix, event schema, propagation latency, failure owner, or seam oracle is present in this window.
items.impact: Consumers may compile independently while disagreeing on runtime, storage, routing, and scheduler truth.
items.builder_discretion: Declare concrete dependency IDs and per-seam request/event/projection contracts with failure and freshness tests.

evidence.exact_quote: This source-preserving standardization keeps the owner and consumer boundaries stated in the original document body. During this batch, `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md` remains the owner doc for the behavior described by its preserved sections, while cross-doc ownership follows the ContractRefs and boundary notes already present in the original text.

items.title: OP-002 acceptance does not falsify owner-boundary drift
items.statement: The unit claims runtime, storage, and scheduler contracts own canonical truth, but its acceptance criteria only restate page identity and labels. They do not test mutation denial, stale projection behavior, conflicting owner truth, command routing, or restart recovery.
items.impact: Generic validators can pass while the GUI becomes a page-local runtime authority.
items.builder_discretion: Add fixtures that inject conflicting/stale owner truth and prove the page cannot mutate canonical enums or scheduler state directly.

evidence.exact_quote: - Orchestrator remains distinct from the UI, CLI, and external providers.

items.title: Host projection authority has a clear stale-state guard
items.statement: OP-028 explicitly keeps mutation semantics with owner systems, forbids a new host tab, and prevents stale projections from authorizing sensitive actions. These are strong authority and misleading-GUI constraints.

items.statement: The unit permits access URL pivots but does not define credential placement, URL redaction, expiry, single-use behavior, principal binding, copy/share restrictions, offline state, network transition behavior, or audit of access launches.
items.impact: A stale or leaked access pivot may expose a host endpoint or mislead an operator during network loss.
items.builder_discretion: Require opaque short-lived launch tokens, owner-side authorization, redacted rendering, expiry states, offline disablement, and access receipts.

items.title: Active host assignments lack race and capacity semantics
items.statement: Active assignments are projected, but no claim/lease identity, capacity limit, concurrent assignment conflict, heartbeat expiry, failover, cancellation, or cleanup receipt is required.
items.impact: Two runs may believe they own the same host capacity or continue displaying an assignment after owner loss.
items.builder_discretion: Bind projections to owner leases with revisions, capacity decisions, expiry, failover, cancellation, and cleanup status.

items.title: Future fixture is not a present acceptance oracle
items.statement: The only behavior-specific validation is deferred to a future fixture. The current index validator cannot prove stale-state denial, owner routing, blocked actions, access security, or receipt linkage.
items.impact: OP-028 can be accepted and indexed without executable evidence for its safety-critical behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Define fixture inputs and expected observable outputs now, including stale, missing, denied, offline, race, and partial-failure cases.

items.title: Record-envelope PlanUnit under-specifies observability
items.statement: OP-003 preserves structural separation but provides no acceptance oracle for correlation IDs, partial receipt visibility, missing-reference diagnostics, support export, or degraded rendering when artifacts are unavailable.
items.impact: Operators cannot distinguish an absent record from a failed artifact fetch or a broken projection.

items.title: Compact inspectors do not impersonate full records
items.statement: The inspector contract keeps summaries compact and routes operators to canonical full records, reducing stale inline duplication and oversized interaction surfaces.

items.title: Compatibility aliases may collide with future canonical routes
items.statement: The excerpt declares several aliases compatibility-only but does not reveal precedence, deprecation, collision detection, telemetry, or migration behavior. It is therefore unknown whether an old alias can shadow a newer canonical route or silently reinterpret imported records.
items.impact: A future route or import family may be captured by a legacy alias with no visible migration warning.
items.builder_discretion: Reserve the alias namespace, define precedence and deprecation telemetry, and fail closed on ambiguous import resolution.

dimension_assessments.summary: Cross-document owner statements and raw source-event flow lack an executable caller/consumer matrix.
Concern and promotion semantics omit illegal-state handling, conflicts, and several guarded transition cases.
Concern mutation, promotion, and host assignment paths lack revision, lease, and idempotency rules.
Record/projection, promotion, routing, and action paths do not define partial-write or partial-success behavior.
Rollback, compensating transitions, retry identity, tombstones, and projection repair remain under-specified.
Host and SCM boundaries include useful guards, but resolver enforcement and restored-route authorization remain undefined.
Paths, evidence refs, records, and access pivots lack redaction, retention, expiry, and deletion rules.
Conflict paths and raw concern sightings lack normalization, sanitization, bounds, and quarantine.
Partial-lineage and stale-host guards are strong, but hidden blocking concerns and failed actions can still look authoritative.
Restarted cross-surface routes and host access pivots have no explicit offline or network-transition state.
Affected-file lists, source-event ingestion, and host capacity have no bounded scale behavior.
Help navigation and concern mutation affordances lack assistive-technology and keyboard acceptance criteria.
Canonical help terms, rationales, errors, and long action text lack locale and RTL rules.
Envelope and route versions, alias precedence, and tombstone migration behavior are not specified.
Operational records lack required revisions, timestamps, correlations, missing-ref diagnostics, and support export behavior.
Dismiss and structural actions lack blocking safety guards and a complete mutation failure/undo contract.
ContractRefs and owner prose are not backed by concrete seam dependencies and propagation oracles in this window.
Current validations are generic or future-facing and do not falsify the safety-critical runtime claims.
Legacy alias collisions and future canonical-route reinterpretation remain an explicit unresolved unknown.
